problem: Write the complex number $z=-1+2\text{i}$ in the form $r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ giving $\theta $ in radians to $3$ decimal places.
worked_solution:
To write our complex number in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $z$ lies in the second quadrant of the complex plane, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{2}{-1})| \\  & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-2)| \\  & ≈2.034.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=\sqrt{5}$ and $\theta =2.034$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=\sqrt{5}\,{\text{e}}^{2.034\,\text{i}}\,.
$$
